CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Judy Gomez is a patient with psoriatic arthritis presenting for follow-up care. She has been tapering her prednisone dose and is currently on 1 mg daily, which she reports is sufficient. She occasionally takes an extra dose approximately once per week when experiencing increased pain in her feet, particularly on days when she is more active despite having a desk job. She reports that methotrexate has been helpful for her joint pain. She previously held a dose of methotrexate during her first COVID-19 vaccination due to concerns about vaccine efficacy, which resulted in severe pain symptoms. She restarted the medication one week later and felt significantly better. She continued methotrexate during her second COVID-19 vaccine dose per telephone hotline guidance. She has also noticed new bruising on her body that appears spontaneously without recalled trauma. She does not feel pain when the bruises form.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
The patient reports joint pain in her feet and knees, which has improved with increased methotrexate dosing. She denies feeling traumatic injury when bruises appear. No other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Psoriatic arthritis.

MEDICATIONS
Prednisone 1 mg daily (to be discontinued).
Methotrexate (current dose not specified).

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
The patient works a desk job. She is more physically active on days off, which worsens her joint pain.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient appears well. Extremities: Feet and ankle joints examined; mild tenderness noted. Knee flexion elicits pain that has improved since increasing methotrexate. Toes demonstrate good range of motion. Nails show ridges consistent with psoriasis.

RESULTS
No laboratory results documented at this visit. Blood work appointment to be scheduled.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Psoriatic arthritis, well-controlled on current regimen. Discontinue prednisone effective today. Continue methotrexate. Bruising likely attributable to prednisone; anticipate improvement with discontinuation. Patient to schedule blood work appointment at front desk prior to leaving. Follow-up appointment in 3 months.
